user: Felix fell off the monkey bars at school yesterday and broke his wrist. How much can we claim from the Meridian policy?
answer:
DearPolicy

Sorry Felix got hurt. For Felix, the policy lists S$600 for “Fractured bones (per Accident) — Simple (closed) fracture” and S$1,500 for “Fractured bones (per Accident) — Compound (open) fracture”; the type must be certified in writing by a registered medical practitioner and confirmed by X-ray, and only one of these benefits is payable for the same bone in the same accident.

A FACT THAT CHANGES THIS ASSESSMENT
Did the broken bone break through the skin, and has the fracture been confirmed by X-ray and certified in writing by a registered medical practitioner?
This changes what your policy pays under: “Items D and E: the type of fracture must be certified in writing by a registered medical practitioner and confirmed by X-ray. Only one of Item D or” (page 1); “4.4 For Items D and E, a Compound fracture means a fracture in which the broken bone breaks through the skin. All” (page 2)

user: I was in hospital after that car accident in March. They admitted me at 9:40pm on 14 March and I was discharged at 8:20am on 18 March. How much hospital cash should Meridian pay me?
answer:
DearPolicy

For you, Meridian’s “Hospital daily allowance” is S$120 per day, up to 60 days per policy year, and its wording counts each complete 24-hour period plus a remaining period of 12 hours or more as another day (page 1; page 2).

Only the insurer decides whether an amount is paid, owed or claimable, after it reviews the claim.

NEXT STEP

Meridian’s claim wording asks for written notice within 30 days of the accident and supporting documents including the hospital discharge summary showing admission and discharge times; check the policy’s claims requirements.

user: Oh, by the way, if one of the kids gets dengue, which of our policies would actually pay anything?
answer:
DearPolicy

For Felix, the SafeStay Family Hospital Cash & Personal Accident Plan is accident-only, so its hospital and medical-expense benefits would not pay for dengue illness (the child hospital daily allowance is currently S$110 per day from 1 July 2026, but only for eligible accident-related confinement).

For Isla, JuniorShield Child Hospital Income Plan lists “Hand, foot & mouth disease or dengue fever hospitalisation (lump sum)” of S$500, so that is the policy benefit specifically relevant to dengue hospitalisation.

I found no dengue-specific benefit for Felix in the policies listed for him; the documents available here may not include every policy the household has.
